blocks.text: At Sabo many in the sangat come with practical grievances and petitions, and the Guru listens to how households are suffering, fields are failing, and protection is still needed in the region. (8–9)
A local notable at Bathinda is then drawn in, given pahul, and turned into an active Singh so that service and defense can be organized on a firmer footing. (10–12)
Bathinda appears here not as a separate political story but as part of the Guru's wider reordering of local authority, discipline, and responsibility after the great disasters. (13–16)
